newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down slightly against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down slightly against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan on Monday continued to fall back on the strength of China's growing foreign exchange reserves, ending at 8.3022 against the U.S. dollar from last Friday's 8.3018, traders said.
On Saturday, China announced its foreign exchange reserves at the end of October totalled $98.8 billion.

Dealers said the central bank was likely to continue to sell yuan for dollars on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market to meet their target of foreign exchange reserves of more than $100 billion by the end of 1996.

The yuan opened slightly higher at 8.3016 and moved up to hit an intra-day high of 8.3012 early in the session. But it then turned and slid down for the rest of the session, hitting a low of 8.3025 several minutes before the close.
Trading was active with most done at about 8.3020, traders said.
"The yuan was actually forced down by some speculative selling on expectation of further falls with possible help from the central bank," one dealer said.
But a second dealer said that falls in the past week, starting last Tuesday, were just a technical correction.
"The yuan will not lose too much as there was a lot of buying at lower levels," he said.
Dealers expect the yuan to rebound on Tuesday.
The yuan closed slightly up at 7.4285 from 7.4500 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0731 from 1.0735 against the Hong Kong dollar.
